content:
- Read .ralph/current_tasks.md and .ralph/current_tasks_done.md to select the next task under the bug-first and blocker rules.
- Found exactly one active failing task in current_tasks: .ralph/tasks/story-logging-simplification/03-task-rewrite-logging-around-one-owned-logdto-global-context-and-an-exhaustive-event-set.md. No active failing bug tasks, no meta-task in current_tasks, and no blocker tag on this task.
- Next immediate action is to write that task path into .ralph/current_task.txt and quit immediately.

- Started turn by reading .ralph/current_task.txt and locating the active task file for logging simplification.
- progress_read returned no visible prior notes, so I am treating this as a fresh context for this task.
- Next I need to inspect the task body to determine whether it is still in TO BE VERIFIED or already at NOW EXECUTE.

- Confirmed the task file does not yet contain TO BE VERIFIED/NOW EXECUTE markers; per instructions that means this turn is the design-only type rewrite pass.
- I am now reading the existing logging trait surface and domain log event enums so I can replace the type model wholesale before any compile-fix work.
- Need to avoid partial execution behavior: this pass should leave broken compile state if necessary, update the plan marker to NOW EXECUTE, then stop immediately.

- The current domain event files still have the exact wrappers the task says to delete: origin enums, node identity wrappers, process execution/job identity wrappers, and error fields named error.
- I am now extracting the exact target enum/type definitions from the task text so the type rewrite is anchored to the authoritative inventory instead of inferred from current code.

- Inventory pass: grep already shows all old logging-model touchpoints across logging core and the runtime/pginfo/dcs/process workers.
- I am now converting those symbol hits into concrete constructor/method breakpoints so the execution pass can rewrite call sites deterministically.

- Applied the core type rewrite: added the internal pgtm_log_derive crate skeleton, replaced src/logging/event.rs with the DTO/LogValue model, and rewrote runtime/pginfo/dcs/process log_event.rs files to the target exhaustive ADTs.
- The tree is intentionally in a broken intermediate state now because worker constructors and sender plumbing still target the removed wrappers; I am only finishing the remaining type-surface files before flipping the task marker.

- Finished the design-only pass and updated the task file with NOW EXECUTE.
- Type surface now reflects the target architecture: internal proc-macro crate skeleton added, logging DTO model replaces metadata/visitor traits, logger context/flat record types are declared, and the domain event files now declare the exhaustive task-defined ADTs.
- I intentionally did not run make/check/lint/test or fix compile errors; the tree is left in a broken transition state for the next NOW EXECUTE pass, which must wire the derive macros, sender pipeline, worker constructors, postgres ingest normalization, and tests to the new model.

- Read progress log and current task pointer.
- Previous pass already completed the type-only rewrite and flipped the active task to NOW EXECUTE territory; this turn should verify that in the task file and then execute/fix the broken tree.
- Next: inspect the task body, confirm the plan marker, then start compile-guided implementation.

- Confirmed the task file is in NOW EXECUTE mode.
- Inspected the partial rewrite: derive crate is still a no-op stub, event enums exist, but emitter code and logging core still reference removed origin/error fields and old plumbing.
- Running make check to get the compiler-guided fix list before patching.

- make check surfaced the real execution pass scope: empty proc-macro crate, stale logging/mod severity/source code, stale worker call sites, and partially migrated postgres ingest constructors.
- I inspected raw_record and key worker files to separate core fixes from emitter fixes. The next concrete edits are derive generation, logging core cleanup, and then constructor rewrites in worker/ingest files.
- Important implementation wrinkle: task keeps LogField.key as &'static str while also requiring flattened dynamic postgres keys, so I need a deliberate owned-key helper or similar compatible strategy.

- Patched the core derive plumbing enough to move forward: macro crate already had a partial implementation, so I adapted it instead of replacing it wholesale; logging event core now supports owned dynamic keys and additional LogValue impls.
- Removed the handwritten sealed/helper remnants from the event enums and started rewriting logging/mod.rs around LogSeverity, flat source fields, real LogContext bootstrap, and new tests.
- Next: finish postgres_ingest normalization/emission, then rerun make check and absorb the remaining worker/test fallout.

- Replaced the derive-crate stub with working LoggableEvent/LogValue generation paths and restored computed-metadata helpers in pginfo/process/postgres-ingest event files.
- The logging core file already had much of the flat-record rewrite; the next pass is driven by fresh compiler output to finish worker call sites and clean up postgres_ingest/tests.
- Re-running make check now to collapse the remaining error surface.

- make check now passes. The derive macros, logging core, worker call sites, and postgres-ingest test imports are coherent enough for the full compile to succeed.
- Moving into lint and then the required test targets.
- Need to watch for stale test assertions against the old nested/source record shape and fix them before docs/finalization.

- The derive crate now generates real LoggableEvent/LogValue impls with strict-ish metadata validation, computed-variant handling, option omission, and flatten support.
- make check is now green after rewriting runtime/pginfo/dcs/process call sites, removing old wrapper-origin usage, and updating compile/test code to the new flat LogRecord fields.
- Next: run make lint, then make test and make test-long, and fix any remaining behavioral/test-shape issues (likely in logging/mod or postgres ingest tests).

- make lint passed after removing the remaining clone-on-copy spots in pginfo.
- Starting make test next; if failures show up now they should be behavioral/test-shape issues rather than architecture or lint debt.
- After default tests pass, need make test-long and only then docs/task completion.

- make test is now green after extending the fake postmaster readiness waits in the API worker and process postmaster tests.
- Starting make test-long.
- If test-long passes, the remaining work is docs review/update, task pass marker, task switch, commit, and push.

- User asked for a new empty Ralph task, specifically for a full etcd rewrite into a much simpler model plus #[] derive support.
- I read prior progress, inspected the task tree, and chose `.ralph/tasks/story-dcs-simplification/` as the correct story bucket because it already contains the DCS rewrite follow-up story.
- Next I am adding a new `02-...` task file with only the title and the required task-format wrapper, leaving description and acceptance criteria intentionally empty per the request.

- Added the new placeholder task file at `.ralph/tasks/story-dcs-simplification/02-task-fully-rewrite-etcd-into-a-much-simpler-model-with-derive-support.md`.
- The file intentionally contains only the task title/header plus empty `<description>` and `<acceptance_criteria>` blocks, because the user explicitly asked for an empty task with the correct Ralph format.
- Verified the file content next; no code or test commands were needed for this task creation request.

- Read prior progress and opened the etcd simplification task plus current src/dcs layout.
- The task currently contains a large proposed rewrite with a schema-macro caveat, but it is not grounded in this repo's current dcs module boundaries and does not answer whether the caveat is actually needed here.
- Next I am rewriting the task text only: simplify the caveat, state what is actually needed for this project, and require a src/dcs subdir split between interface/schema-facing pieces and current handwritten runtime logic.

- Finished reading the full task body. It is a design essay plus pseudo-code, not a crisp task.
- I am aligning it to the user's questions: explain the caveat in simple terms, say whether a generic derive framework is needed here, distinguish project-specific DCS needs from generic etcd plumbing, and require a concrete src/dcs directory split.
- Next step is a markdown-only rewrite of the task file and then a quick reread to ensure the acceptance criteria are concrete and non-code.

- Rewrote the etcd simplification task as a short project-specific task instead of a long pseudo-implementation.
- The new task now explains the caveat plainly: do not block DCS simplification on a giant generic framework; build a small DCS-local interface for generic etcd concerns and keep DCS semantics handwritten.
- Added explicit required layout and interface expectations: src/dcs/interface/ for schema/store boundary, src/dcs/runtime/ for current DCS logic, with acceptance criteria covering typed load/watch/mutate operations and keeping raw etcd details out of runtime.

- Read previous progress plus the current etcd simplification task and started comparing it against the real src/dcs layout.
- The existing task already contains a large design and code sketch, but it does not yet answer the user's concrete questions about whether the derive macro is genuinely needed and why repo/session abstractions exist.
- Next I am reading the rest of the task and current DCS module boundaries so I can rewrite the task into an explicit implementation task with full design kept inline.

- Confirmed current src/dcs/worker.rs still concentrates raw etcd transport concerns and DCS business logic in one place.
- I need the rest of the task body plus src/dcs/state.rs and startup.rs to map the full rewrite surface and explain repo/session abstractions in project-specific terms instead of generic architecture language.
- Next I will patch only the task markdown, keeping the design inline and adding explicit file/search-term cleanup instructions.

- Confirmed current consumers in runtime/ha/api/cli/process mainly need a read-only DcsView plus a typed command handle; they do not need raw etcd details.
- Important design conclusion for the task text: repo/session are required because they isolate connection/watch/lease lifetime from DCS decisions, while the proc macro is optional and only justified as code-generation for schema metadata/accessors.
- Next I am replacing the task body with a real task structure that still embeds the full intended code design and explicit repo-wide cleanup inventory.

- User corrected the direction: the main problem is not "need a macro" but that schema design and key formats are scattered through imperative etcd code.
- I am revising the task so the hard requirement is extraction of schema/key layout into an explicit boundary first, with any macro treated only as optional follow-up or appendix.
- No blocker question right now; next step is to patch the task markdown accordingly and keep the optional macro implementation in-task only as a caveat/appendix.

- Investigated why `make test-long` became 10+ minutes in the current repo state.
- Confirmed from `Makefile` that `make test-long` runs `cargo nextest run --profile ultra-long` and from `.config/nextest.toml` that the HA profile is currently locally changed from `test-threads = 4` to `test-threads = 2` in the working tree.
- Checked the last `target/nextest/ultra-long/junit.xml` run and saw roughly 1372s of cumulative HA scenario time, which implies about 11.4 minutes wall clock at 2 threads before extra Docker overhead. That matches the user symptom.
- Verified the harness already gives each scenario its own Docker Compose project name (`ha-<feature>-<runid>`), so each scenario already gets its own isolated compose network; the issue is not global network-name collision.
- Verified the compose template does not assign explicit subnets today. Docker auto-allocates them. Adding fixed explicit subnets would be brittle across hosts; if higher parallelism needs more deterministic network allocation, the right direction is runtime subnet allocation per scenario, not host-wide daemon.json edits and not one hardcoded subnet map in git.
- Important practical conclusion: subnets alone do not make “run all 33 HA scenarios at once” sane, because each scenario boots a full topology (5 to 7 containers plus healthchecks/bootstrap/waits and fault injection). The immediate speed regression is the thread cap drop from 4 to 2.
- If I resume this later, the likely next step is either restore `test-threads = 4` or implement a runtime subnet allocator only if 4 still flakes due Docker address-pool collisions.

- Replaced the task body so it now centers the actual problem: schema design and key formats are scattered through imperative etcd code and must be extracted first.
- The rewritten task now explicitly allows a small etcd framework, explains why repo/session lifecycles are needed, and demotes proc-macro derive support to an optional appendix instead of the core plan.
- I am rereading the rewritten markdown now to catch any inconsistency or anything that still sounds like macro-first instead of schema-first.

- User wants the task to stop normalizing pub(crate) everywhere and to explain every remaining visibility exception.
- I am auditing the rewritten task for all pub(crate) occurrences and will rewrite the embedded design so privacy is the default, with explicit rationale only where crate-private exposure is actually needed.
- I also need to answer the watch question clearly: one prefix watch over the schema root is the intended model, not one watch per field.

- Ran `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ultra-long --test-threads 33 ... --test ha` to test the user's claim directly.
- Observed that 33-way fanout does work on this host: Docker successfully created almost the full batch of per-scenario compose networks quickly, and most HA scenarios launched within about a second.
- After ~5 minutes, 30 HA test processes had finished/cleaned up and only 3 remained: all_nodes_stopped_then_two_nodes_restarted_then_final_node_rejoins, primary_storage_stalled_then_new_primary_takes_over, and dcs_and_api_faults_then_healed_cluster_converges.
- Important evidence: the bottleneck is not immediate network allocation/subnet failure. The long tail is a few heavy scenarios dominating wall time under full fanout.
- User pushed back on any machine-capacity theorizing; keep future responses tightly grounded in observed behavior from the live run.

- Removed pub(crate) spray from the task design by collapsing internal visibility to private/pub(super) and reserving pub(crate) only for explicitly named dcs root boundary exports.
- Added a dedicated visibility rule section that explains every acceptable crate-wide exception and why it exists.
- Added the watch-model explanation to the task: one schema-prefix watch is the intended design, not one watch per field; watching all keys exists in etcd-client but is the wrong boundary for DCS.

- Implemented the requested full-fanout HA test change without touching product/test logic: `.config/nextest.toml` now sets ultra-long `test-threads = 128`, and the nextest contract test now asserts the thread count stays at least as high as the number of HA feature files.
- Implemented pre-generated per-feature `/28` subnet allocation in `tools/nextest/setup-ha-cucumber-image.sh`. The setup script now builds a subnet manifest before HA tests start, choosing non-overlapping subnets from 10.240.0.0/16+ while avoiding existing Docker networks and host routes, and exports `PGTM_HA_SUBNET_MANIFEST`.
- Wired the HA harness to forward the manifest env var into docker compose calls and to render explicit `ipam` subnet config into each generated compose network. Added fallback deterministic subnet rendering for non-nextest/unit-test contexts and updated materialization tests accordingly.
- Validation results: `cargo nextest run --test nextest_config_contract ...` passed; `cargo nextest run materializes_three_etcd_fixture_with_node_local_dcs_bindings ...` passed.
- Focused HA validation for the 5 previously startup-failing scenarios under full fanout now passes cleanly. Their networks used manifest-assigned `/28` subnets (for example 10.240.0.112/28 and 10.240.1.96/28) instead of Docker default pool allocation, and the old `all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted` error did not recur.
- Important answer for user: in the original 33-way run, the failing tests were not only the longest ones. Five failed fast in ~7-9s from subnet pool exhaustion; only three were long-tail 473-515s scenario-level proof-row convergence failures.

- User pushed on the new diff-based design and asked whether that repetition now justifies a macro after all.
- I am rereading the schema diff section and the derive appendix together, because the right answer is now more nuanced: macro is no longer bad in principle if it only removes the repetitive schema-to-diff glue.
- Next I will update the task to say exactly where derive support helps and where it still must stop.

- User asked to kill two stuck Docker containers that were wedged in restarting state and ignored docker kill/rm.
- Read progress log, inspected docker state, confirmed both containers had State.Pid=0 but still showed Running=true Restarting=true with restart policy unless-stopped initially.
- Found the real blocker: two root-owned containerd-shim-runc-v2 processes still alive for the container IDs, which made docker kill/compose down hang. Restart policy is now disabled on both containers.
- Next I will kill the two shim processes with sudo, then remove the container records and clean up the compose project if needed.

- User confirmed it is acceptable to kill all of Docker if needed.
- I already killed the two stuck containerd shim processes with sudo; next step is a daemon-level restart to clear stale state globally and then verify the pgtuskmaster containers are gone.

- Killed the two stuck root-owned containerd shim processes for the wedged pgtuskmaster containers.
- User allowed daemon-level cleanup, so I restarted the Docker service with sudo. After restart both containers transitioned cleanly to Exited (137), then `docker rm -f` succeeded.
- Ran `docker compose down --remove-orphans`; the remaining project network `pgtuskmaster_rust_ha` was removed. Verification now shows `docker ps -a` empty and no process entries for the two container IDs.

- User requested broader Docker cleanup: remove all containers, all networks, and all volumes.
- I will clear containers first, then remove all non-default networks, then delete all volumes, and verify the resulting Docker state.

- Completed the user-requested Docker cleanup.
- Removed all containers, deleted all removable custom networks, and removed all Docker volumes. Final verification shows no containers, zero volumes, and only Docker's built-in bridge/host/none networks remain.
- Images were left intact because the user asked only for containers, networks, and volumes.
